DeWitt Residence

A long, low house and garage under one shed roof, looking out over the Strait toward Victoria and the San Juan Islands.

StructuralTo be engaged in next phase

A note from Sparrow

This is a simple-looking house that asks a lot of its builder. One big shed roof ties the house, breezeway and garage together. The whole north side opens up to the water. Inside it's exposed concrete and white oak, and outside it's black siding and steel. When there are this few materials, every joint shows. That's the kind of work we like best.

We work cost-plus and open book. This estimate is our first pass from the pricing set. Pre-construction is where we turn it into a real budget together.

Mike StuntzOwner, Sparrow Woodworks
01  The project

One roof, one long view

About 1,810 heated square feet plus a two-car garage, set on pin piles on a sloped, landslide-mapped lot. The house, an open breezeway and the garage share one 112-foot SIPS roof that pitches down to the south.

02  Who we are

Hands-on where it matters most

At Sparrow, our own people handle the parts of a build that matter most. Our carpenters frame and set the structure. Our wood shop builds the pieces you'll see and touch every day. On the DeWitt house, that starts with the white oak casework, interior doors and ceiling details. We take pride in the craft and the attention we bring to every project.

fill in: shop photo

Open book, cost-plus

You see every invoice and every hour. Our fee is a fixed percentage, so we're on the same side of the budget.

Our own crews since 2011

Framing, structure, siding, trim and casework are done by Sparrow people, not passed down a chain of subs.

Peninsula ground

We build across Kitsap, Jefferson and Clallam counties. We've priced the drive and the lodging into this number.

AIA National, AIA Seattle and Architizer A+ awards with our architect partners, 2023 to 2025.

What we caught in the pricing set

  1. Septic vs. bedroom count. Septic is permitted for two bedrooms. The plan has a main bedroom, a guest bedroom and an office. Worth confirming the county won't count the office as a bedroom.
  2. Berm against framed walls. The south side is bermed against the guest bedroom and main bedroom/office. A-601 has no below-grade wall type there. We priced concrete stem walls up to berm height.
  3. Window energy values. A-602 lists default U-values. Defaults won't pass the energy code. Kolbe's NFRC numbers need to go on the schedule.
  4. Hot tub. The renderings show the tub on grade off the main bedroom, but it isn't on the plans, and the patio around it is N.I.C. It still needs a level pad, a power run and a spot for the equipment. We carried those.
  5. Spec cleanups. The garage doors have no product listed. The memo lists the guest bath twice. The roofing is labeled 'to match existing' on a new house.

04  Value options

Ways to save without touching the design

Each option keeps the roof, the glass and the white oak. Prices include markups and tax.

−$19,312

Domestic charred cedar siding

Swap Nakamoto Suyaki for a domestic charred or black-oiled cedar shiplap with the same look. The memo allows it.

−$11,638

Domestic T&G at soffits and walls

Use a domestic thermally modified or clear cedar 1x6 T&G in place of Lunawood Luna Layer at soffits and interior walls.

−$7,352

Drywall ceilings in guest room and office

Keep the white oak ceilings in the main living spaces. Use painted drywall in the guest bedroom and office, like the primary bedroom.

−$21,296

Fiber cement fascia and corners

Black prefinished fiber cement or painted fir in place of Richlite at the fascia, rakes, corners and window heads.

Current$2,938,235
All four options−$59,599
New total$2,878,635

About 14 months on site

06  Pre-construction

Working it out before we break ground

Pre-construction is where SHED, the engineers and our team work out how this house actually gets built on this site. Access, piles and the roof are the big ones. It's also where this estimate becomes a budget you can trust.

  1. 1

    Drawing review

    Constructability review of each design phase with SHED and the engineers, focused on site access, piles and the SIPS roof.

  2. 2

    Trade bids and budget

    Real bids from piles, concrete, roofing, mechanical and electrical, rolled into an open-book budget.

  3. 3

    Shop drawings

    Drawings for everything we build in our shop: casework, oak doors, ceiling details and benches.

  4. 4

    Long-lead ordering and schedule

    Kolbe windows, SIPS, Nakamoto siding and Lunawood ordered on time, with a schedule built around them.

  5. 5

    Cost-plus construction agreement

    A clear agreement with our fee, allowances and reporting spelled out.
